paragraphs.title: Moses and Aaron Ask Pharaoh to Release the People

easy.question: Who came to Pharaoh?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Moses and Joshua
Aaron and Caleb
easy.explanation: The first verse says that Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh.

easy.question: What did Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to do?
answers: Give them gold
Send the people of Israel away
Build a new city
easy.explanation: They said to Pharaoh, “Let my people go.”

easy.question: Who said, “I know not the Lord”?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Pharaoh said that he did not know the Lord.

medium.question: Why did Moses and Aaron ask to travel three days into the wilderness?
answers: To sacrifice to the Lord
To find water
To build a palace
medium.explanation: They asked to go into the wilderness to sacrifice to the Lord their God.

medium.question: How did Pharaoh respond to the request to let Israel go?
answers: He agreed immediately
He refused to let them go
He asked to join them
medium.explanation: Pharaoh explicitly said, “Neither will I let Israel go.”

medium.question: What did Moses and Aaron say might happen if they did not go and sacrifice?
answers: They might be struck by plague or the sword
They would lose their homes
They would be forced to build a palace
medium.explanation: They warned that the Lord might strike them with pestilence or the sword.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the request to travel only three days into the wilderness?
answers: The immediate purpose was to worship the Lord in the wilderness
Israel already wanted to leave Egypt permanently
Moses did not know where to go
challenge.explanation: The request is presented as a journey for the immediate purpose of sacrificing to the Lord, not merely as aimless escape.

challenge.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in Moses and Aaron’s words?
answers: If Pharaoh let Israel go, they would build him a city
If they could not go and sacrifice, plague or the sword might strike them
If they went into the wilderness, Pharaoh would become king
challenge.explanation: They warned that if they could not worship the Lord, disease or the sword might strike them.

challenge.question: What does the use of the titles “God of Israel” and “God of the Hebrews” emphasize?
answers: The speakers presented the Lord as the God of their people and of Israel
There were two different gods
Pharaoh already knew the Lord well
challenge.explanation: Both titles refer to the same God and emphasize his connection with the people of Israel, also called the Hebrews.

questions.question: What can we infer from the request to travel only three days into the wilderness?
answers: The immediate purpose was to worship the Lord in the wilderness
Israel already wanted to leave Egypt permanently
Moses did not know where to go
questions.explanation: The request is presented as a journey for the immediate purpose of sacrificing to the Lord, not merely as aimless escape.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in Moses and Aaron’s words?
answers: If Pharaoh let Israel go, they would build him a city
If they could not go and sacrifice, plague or the sword might strike them
If they went into the wilderness, Pharaoh would become king
questions.explanation: They warned that if they could not worship the Lord, disease or the sword might strike them.

questions.question: What does the use of the titles “God of Israel” and “God of the Hebrews” emphasize?
answers: The speakers presented the Lord as the God of their people and of Israel
There were two different gods
Pharaoh already knew the Lord well
questions.explanation: Both titles refer to the same God and emphasize his connection with the people of Israel, also called the Hebrews.

easy.question: Who asked Moses and Aaron why they were interrupting the people’s work?
answers: Pharaoh
One of the officers
One of the Israelites
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that Pharaoh asked Moses and Aaron why they were interrupting the people.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh command them to stop giving the people?
answers: Water
Straw
Bricks
easy.explanation: Pharaoh commanded them to stop giving the people straw for making bricks.

easy.question: Who commanded the taskmasters and officers to increase the workload?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that Pharaoh gave this command to the taskmasters and officers.

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh decide to increase the Israelites’ labor?
answers: He thought they were idle and were using the request as an excuse
Egypt had run out of bricks
He wanted to give them a vacation
medium.explanation: Pharaoh said they were idle and thought that hard work would keep them from listening to Moses and Aaron.

medium.question: In the phrase “Why do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works?”, what does “let ... from their works” mean?
answers: Praise the people
Distract the people from their work
Gather the people for battle
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means to interrupt or distract the people from their labor.

medium.question: What sequence of commands did Pharaoh give?
answers: Stop the work, provide straw, and reduce the brick quota
Provide straw, reduce the work, and then release the people
Stop providing straw, keep the same brick quota, and increase the labor
medium.explanation: Pharaoh commanded them to stop providing straw, keep the same number of bricks, and increase the labor.

challenge.question: What central difficulty did Pharaoh’s command create?
answers: The people had to make the same number of bricks without being given straw
The people received straw but were forbidden to make bricks
The people had to make fewer bricks with more straw
challenge.explanation: They had to maintain the same quota while gathering the straw themselves.

challenge.question: What did Pharaoh hope to accomplish by increasing the labor?
answers: The people would learn to build faster
The people would be too busy to listen to Moses and Aaron
The people would receive higher wages
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh wanted hard labor to keep the people from paying attention to Moses and Aaron’s words.

challenge.question: In the verse, what does “as heretofore” mean?
answers: Only yesterday
Only three days ago
As before, up to that time
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the previous customary situation, not necessarily to exactly two days.

questions.question: What central difficulty did Pharaoh’s command create?
answers: The people had to make the same number of bricks without being given straw
The people received straw but were forbidden to make bricks
The people had to make fewer bricks with more straw
questions.explanation: They had to maintain the same quota while gathering the straw themselves.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh hope to accomplish by increasing the labor?
answers: The people would learn to build faster
The people would be too busy to listen to Moses and Aaron
The people would receive higher wages
questions.explanation: Pharaoh wanted hard labor to keep the people from paying attention to Moses and Aaron’s words.

questions.question: In the verse, what does “as heretofore” mean?
answers: Only yesterday
Only three days ago
As before, up to that time
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the previous customary situation, not necessarily to exactly two days.

paragraphs.title: The People Search for Straw and Fail to Meet the Quota

easy.question: Who told the Israelites that Pharaoh would not give them straw?
answers: Pharaoh
Moses
The officers of Israel
easy.explanation: The taskmasters and officers told the people that Pharaoh would not give them straw.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites search for straw?
answers: In Canaan
Throughout the land of Egypt
In Pharaoh’s palace
easy.explanation: The people scattered throughout Egypt to gather straw.

easy.question: Whom did the taskmasters beat when the quota was not completed?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Pharaoh
The officers of the Israelites
easy.explanation: The taskmasters beat the officers of the Israelites, who were responsible for the people.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites have to gather straw?
answers: Because Pharaoh had stopped giving it to them
Because they wanted to leave Egypt
Because Moses commanded them to
medium.explanation: Pharaoh no longer gave them straw, yet he still required them to make the same number of bricks.

medium.question: What did the taskmasters do after the Israelites went to gather straw?
answers: They stopped the work
They urged the people to complete the daily quota
They gave the people new straw
medium.explanation: The taskmasters demanded that the people complete their daily work as when straw had been provided.

medium.question: In the verse, what were the taskmasters?
answers: Spiritual leaders
Messengers who brought straw
Supervisors who drove the people to work
medium.explanation: They pressed the people to work and beat the officers, so they were supervisors enforcing the labor.

challenge.question: What resulted from Pharaoh’s demand that the work not be reduced even without straw?
answers: The burden of labor on the Israelites became heavier
The Israelites worked less
The taskmasters canceled the quota
challenge.explanation: The people had to gather straw themselves and still make the same number of bricks.

challenge.question: In the phrase “as when there was straw,” what comparison is being made?
answers: The work should be done tomorrow evening
The daily work should be completed as in the earlier days
The work should be completed before the Exodus
challenge.explanation: The officers were required to complete the same quota they had completed on previous days when straw was available.

challenge.question: What can we infer about the role of the officers of Israel?
answers: They were members of Pharaoh’s family
They only gathered straw
They were responsible for ensuring that the people completed their work
challenge.explanation: The taskmasters held them responsible for the quota, so they were beaten when the work was not completed.

questions.question: What resulted from Pharaoh’s demand that the work not be reduced even without straw?
answers: The burden of labor on the Israelites became heavier
The Israelites worked less
The taskmasters canceled the quota
questions.explanation: The people had to gather straw themselves and still make the same number of bricks.

questions.question: In the phrase “as when there was straw,” what comparison is being made?
answers: The work should be done tomorrow evening
The daily work should be completed as in the earlier days
The work should be completed before the Exodus
questions.explanation: The officers were required to complete the same quota they had completed on previous days when straw was available.

questions.question: What can we infer about the role of the officers of Israel?
answers: They were members of Pharaoh’s family
They only gathered straw
They were responsible for ensuring that the people completed their work
questions.explanation: The taskmasters held them responsible for the quota, so they were beaten when the work was not completed.

paragraphs.title: The Officers of Israel Complain to Pharaoh

easy.question: Who came and cried out to Pharaoh?
answers: The officers of the Israelites
Moses and Aaron
The Egyptian officials
easy.explanation: The verse says that the officers of the Israelites came and cried out to Pharaoh.

easy.question: What did the officers complain about?
answers: They had no water
They were given no straw but were still required to make bricks
They were not allowed to leave Egypt
easy.explanation: They said they were given no straw, yet were still commanded to make the same number of bricks.

easy.question: How did Pharaoh respond to their complaint?
answers: He gave them time off
He reduced the brick quota
He called them idle and told them to keep working
easy.explanation: Pharaoh rejected their complaint, accused them of idleness, and ordered them to continue working.

medium.question: Why did the officers of Israel approach Pharaoh?
answers: They were given no straw but were still required to make bricks
Pharaoh had canceled their work
They wanted to become Egyptian officers
medium.explanation: They approached Pharaoh because the working conditions had changed: the straw was withheld, but the brick quota remained.

medium.question: In Pharaoh’s words, “Ye are idle, ye are idle,” what does “idle” mean?
answers: Sad
Lazy or inactive
Strong
medium.explanation: Pharaoh accused them of being lazy and using the desire to sacrifice as an excuse.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence of events?
answers: The officers received straw, complained, and Pharaoh praised them
Pharaoh released Israel, and then they made bricks
The officers complained, Pharaoh rejected them, and they realized their situation had become worse
medium.explanation: They first cried out to Pharaoh, then he accused them of idleness, and afterward they realized their situation was worse.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “your daily tasks” emphasize?
answers: They had to provide the required amount every day
They were allowed to work only once a week
They had to make bricks only at night
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the daily quota could not be reduced even when straw was withheld.

challenge.question: Why did the officers realize that they were in a bad situation after speaking with Pharaoh?
answers: Pharaoh sent them out of the land
They remained responsible for the brick quota without receiving straw
They were no longer officers
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh did not ease their burden; he kept the quota in place, increasing their pressure and responsibility.

challenge.question: What is the central contradiction in Pharaoh’s words to the officers?
answers: He claimed they were rich even though they were princes
He claimed they were free even though they worked
He called them idle even though they had to work hard without straw
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh interpreted their request to sacrifice as idleness, although they were being forced to work harder without straw.

questions.question: What does the phrase “your daily tasks” emphasize?
answers: They had to provide the required amount every day
They were allowed to work only once a week
They had to make bricks only at night
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the daily quota could not be reduced even when straw was withheld.

questions.question: Why did the officers realize that they were in a bad situation after speaking with Pharaoh?
answers: Pharaoh sent them out of the land
They remained responsible for the brick quota without receiving straw
They were no longer officers
questions.explanation: Pharaoh did not ease their burden; he kept the quota in place, increasing their pressure and responsibility.

questions.question: What is the central contradiction in Pharaoh’s words to the officers?
answers: He claimed they were rich even though they were princes
He claimed they were free even though they worked
He called them idle even though they had to work hard without straw
questions.explanation: Pharaoh interpreted their request to sacrifice as idleness, although they were being forced to work harder without straw.

paragraphs.title: The Israelites Blame Moses and Aaron

easy.question: Whom did the people meet as they came out from Pharaoh?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Pharaoh and his servants
The Israelites in the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says that they met Moses and Aaron as they came out from Pharaoh.

easy.question: When did they meet them?
answers: Before they went to Pharaoh
As they came out from Pharaoh
After they reached the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says they met Moses and Aaron as they came out from Pharaoh.

easy.question: What did the people ask the Lord to do to Moses and Aaron?
answers: Bless them
Send them into the wilderness
Look upon them and judge them
easy.explanation: They said, “The Lord look upon you, and judge,” asking the Lord to judge them.

medium.question: Why did the people blame Moses and Aaron?
answers: They believed Moses and Aaron had made Pharaoh and his servants hate them more
They had taken Pharaoh’s sword
They had refused to leave Egypt
medium.explanation: They claimed that Moses and Aaron had made them detestable in the eyes of Pharaoh and his servants.

medium.question: In the phrase “ye have made our savour to be abhorred,” what does it mean?
answers: You made our clothes wet
You caused us to be disliked or dishonored
You prepared bad food for us
medium.explanation: The context shows that they meant Moses and Aaron had made them appear hateful or contemptible, not merely given them a bad smell.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Moses and Aaron met the people, then left Pharaoh
The people gave Pharaoh a sword, then spoke with Moses
The people met Moses and Aaron as they left Pharaoh, then blamed them
medium.explanation: First they met Moses and Aaron as they came from Pharaoh, and then they made their complaint.

challenge.question: What do the words “The Lord look upon you, and judge” reveal about the speakers’ feelings?
answers: They were very pleased with Moses and Aaron
They were angry and felt they had been wronged
They did not know who had spoken to them
challenge.explanation: Appealing to the Lord to judge them expresses complaint, anger, and a sense of injustice.

challenge.question: According to the complainants, who might put a sword in their hands to kill them?
answers: Moses and Aaron
The people in the wilderness
Pharaoh and his servants
challenge.explanation: They said that being hated by Pharaoh and his servants could lead to a sword being used against them.

challenge.question: Why do the complainants’ words express cause and effect?
answers: They claimed that Moses and Aaron’s mission had caused Pharaoh to treat them more harshly
They claimed that Pharaoh had already released the people
They claimed that the sword disappeared after Moses left
challenge.explanation: They believed Moses and Aaron’s actions had made them despised by Pharaoh and his servants, putting their lives at risk.

questions.question: What do the words “The Lord look upon you, and judge” reveal about the speakers’ feelings?
answers: They were very pleased with Moses and Aaron
They were angry and felt they had been wronged
They did not know who had spoken to them
questions.explanation: Appealing to the Lord to judge them expresses complaint, anger, and a sense of injustice.

questions.question: According to the complainants, who might put a sword in their hands to kill them?
answers: Moses and Aaron
The people in the wilderness
Pharaoh and his servants
questions.explanation: They said that being hated by Pharaoh and his servants could lead to a sword being used against them.

questions.question: Why do the complainants’ words express cause and effect?
answers: They claimed that Moses and Aaron’s mission had caused Pharaoh to treat them more harshly
They claimed that Pharaoh had already released the people
They claimed that the sword disappeared after Moses left
questions.explanation: They believed Moses and Aaron’s actions had made them despised by Pharaoh and his servants, putting their lives at risk.

paragraphs.title: Moses Cries Out to the Lord

easy.question: Who returned to the Lord?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And Moses returned unto the Lord.”

easy.question: To whom did Moses speak?
answers: Pharaoh
The Lord
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Moses spoke to the Lord, as shown by his words, “Lord.”

easy.question: What did Moses say had still not been done for the people?
answers: Aaron had not been sent to him
They had not spoken with Pharaoh
The people had not been delivered
easy.explanation: Moses said, “Neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.”

medium.question: What happened to the people after Moses came to Pharaoh to speak in the Lord’s name?
answers: The people were treated worse
The people left Egypt
Pharaoh released the people
medium.explanation: Moses said that Pharaoh had done evil to the people after he came to him.

medium.question: In the question “Why hast thou so evil entreated this people?”, what does “evil entreated” mean?
answers: Rescued
Treated harshly or caused harm
Called
medium.explanation: The phrase means to treat someone badly or make the situation worse.

medium.question: Why did Moses ask, “Why is it that thou hast sent me?”
answers: He wanted to be king
He did not want to speak with the people
His mission had not yet brought deliverance and had made the people suffer
medium.explanation: Moses saw that the people were suffering more since his mission began and had not yet been delivered.

challenge.question: What contrast between Moses’ mission and its result does he emphasize?
answers: He came to speak in the Lord’s name, but Pharaoh harmed the people and no deliverance came
He came to speak with the people, but they refused to listen
He came to free Pharaoh, but Moses was imprisoned
challenge.explanation: Moses says that although he spoke in the Lord’s name, the people’s condition became worse and deliverance did not come.

challenge.question: What does “since” mean in “For since I came to Pharaoh”?
answers: The events happened before Moses was sent
The situation began after Moses came to Pharaoh
The situation began only after the Exodus
challenge.explanation: “Since” identifies the point in time after which the situation Moses describes began.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the phrase “thy people”?
answers: Moses viewed the Israelites as his property
Pharaoh owned the people
The Israelites were the Lord’s people
challenge.explanation: Moses addressed the Lord as the one to whom the Israelites belonged.

questions.question: What contrast between Moses’ mission and its result does he emphasize?
answers: He came to speak in the Lord’s name, but Pharaoh harmed the people and no deliverance came
He came to speak with the people, but they refused to listen
He came to free Pharaoh, but Moses was imprisoned
questions.explanation: Moses says that although he spoke in the Lord’s name, the people’s condition became worse and deliverance did not come.

questions.question: What does “since” mean in “For since I came to Pharaoh”?
answers: The events happened before Moses was sent
The situation began after Moses came to Pharaoh
The situation began only after the Exodus
questions.explanation: “Since” identifies the point in time after which the situation Moses describes began.

questions.question: What can we understand from the phrase “thy people”?
answers: Moses viewed the Israelites as his property
Pharaoh owned the people
The Israelites were the Lord’s people
questions.explanation: Moses addressed the Lord as the one to whom the Israelites belonged.
